title: An Investigation of Stabilization Scaling in Finite-Strain Virtual Element Methods for Hyperelasticity
summary: Low-order virtual element methods (VEM) compute a consistent finite-strain contribution through polynomial projections and rely on stabilization to control the unresolved modes in the projector kernel. In current hyperelastic VEM practice, stabilization is often defined by integrating a nonlinear surrogate energy over an auxiliary sub-triangulation and scaled through modified Lamé parameters and incompressibility factors; this can introduce sensitivity to the arbitrary internal tessellation, complicate consistent Newton linearization, and, most critically, inject bulk-dependent proxies into…
